question: Is context-subgraph supervision for triple/path training genuinely novel, or is it already covered by subgraph-based KGQA, graph-RAG, and KG-completion subgraph retrieval methods (DrKGC, GRAG, GNN-RAG, SG-RAG)?
description: Subgraph retrieval-augmentation is a well-populated area at inference time; the open question is whether the specific framing of enriching the TRAINING supervision signal (not just retrieval at test time) with co-passage triples is differentiated.
confidence_basis: Based on full-text reads of DrKGC and GNN-RAG and abstracts of GRAG/SG-RAG/UniKGQA; a targeted search for training-time multi-triple supervision was not yet run.
rationale: Novelty cannot be claimed until the closest subgraph-augmentation work is read and its overlap with training-time context enrichment is assessed.
resolution: Partially resolved: the closest retrieved subgraph-augmentation work constructs context at inference time (GNN-RAG retrieves shortest paths for prompt context; SG-RAG MOT merges/orders retrieved triplets; GRAG retrieves textual subgraphs) or learns a query-specific subgraph at inference with a GCN adapter integrated into a prompt during LLM fine-tuning (DrKGC). None of them derives context from the source passage of the supervision triple. So context-subgraph retrieval per se is not novel, but passage-derived, training-supervision-level context enrichment was not found in the retrieved set. The distinction from DrKGC is narrow and must be argued explicitly.
